tenses: Simple = facts and habits · continuous (be + -ing) = in progress · perfect (have + participle) = connected to a later moment.
verbs: Most verbs just add -ed. Irregular ones change: go → went → gone. Column 2 is the past (I went), column 3 goes after have (I've gone).
mistakes: The big ones: I'm 30 (not "I have 30"), I agree (not "I'm agree"), explain to me (not "explain me"). Notice them, don't panic.
place: in = inside a space · on = on a surface or a line · at = a point, or where something happens.
usedto: used to + verb = past habit (solía) · be used to + -ing = it's normal for you · get used to + -ing = it's becoming normal.
passive: be + past participle. Use it when the action matters more than who did it: My phone was stolen.
reported: Move the verb one step back: "I am tired" → She said she was tired. Say something · tell someone something.
be: be = ser and estar. Use it for age and feelings too: I'm 30, I'm hungry (not "I have").
modals: Modal + base verb, with no to, -s or -ed: She can swim. can = ability · should = advice · must = obligation · might = maybe.
domake: do = activities and tasks (do homework) · make = create or produce something (make dinner, make a decision).
time: in = long periods (in May) · on = days and dates (on Monday) · at = exact times (at 3:00). Nothing before next, last, this or every.
tofor: to = destination, who receives it, purpose + verb (I'm here to learn) · for = benefit, duration, purpose + noun (for dinner).
pronouns: Same person, different job: I · me · my · mine · myself. Don't mix up your/you're, its/it's, their/they're.
quantity: Can you count it? Countable → many, a few. Uncountable (water, advice, money) → much, a little. A lot of works for both.
frequency: always, usually, often, never go before the main verb but after be: I always study · He is always late.
conversation: Answer, add a little extra, then ask something back. That's the whole trick.
linking: Learn one or two from each group and actually use them. With however or therefore: period or semicolon before, comma after.
false: They look like Spanish but mean something else: actually ≠ actualmente · embarrassed ≠ embarazada · library ≠ librería.
basics: English always needs a subject and likes the order Subject + Verb + Object: It's raining · She reads a book.
summary: What it was → main idea → 2–3 details → your reaction → what you didn't get.
stuck: Stay in English: describe it (It's a kind of…), buy time (Let me think…) or ask (How do you say…?).
opinions: I think… · I see your point, but… · I'm not sure about that. Disagree with the idea, not the person.
conditionals: If + present, will = real future · If + past, would = imaginary · If + had done, would have = past that didn't happen. Never will or would in the if part.
perfect: Do you say when? → past simple (I went last year). Life until now, no time → present perfect (I've been there twice).
gerund: -ing after prepositions and verbs like enjoy, avoid, finish · to + verb after want, need, decide, hope.
phrasal: Verb + small word = a new meaning. Learn them as one word: look for = buscar · find out = averiguar.
compare: Short adjectives: -er / the -est (cheaper, the cheapest). Long ones: more / the most. good → better → the best.
pronunciation: The stressed syllable is the loudest one. Get the stress right and people understand you, accent and all.
numbers: English uses a point for decimals and commas for thousands: 1.5 = one point five · 10,000 = ten thousand.
email: Start friendly, say why you're writing, ask clearly, and close with a next step.
